newsitem.title: USA: Dell says well-positioned for second half.
newsitem.headline: Dell says well-positioned for second half.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp, reporting a 108-percent jump in net income for the second quarter, said Tuesday it is well-positioned for the second half of the year.

"We believe we are well-positioned to take advantage of favorable industry conditions," said chief executive Michael Dell in a statement. "We will remain focused on our goal of taking our direct business model to the next level, helping customers benefit from ... the internet, value-added services and workstations."

Dell Tuesday reported a $214 million net income, or $0.59 a share, on revenues of $2.81 billion in the second quarter ended August 3. This compared with a $103 million net, or $0.28 a share, on $1.69 billion in sales in the 1996 quarter.
A First Call poll of 34 analysts had put the computer maker's earnings at $0.54 a share.
Dell said revenue growth outpaced unit growth in the quarter and the average system selling price was higher than a year ago.

"Clearly our customers are purchasing more richly configured systems, as they realize the benefits of our direct business model," Dell said. The computer maker's gross margin rose to 22.2 percent in the quarter from 21.6 percent in the first quarter.

Dell said sales in the Americas, which made up 71 percent of its total revenues, increased 74 percent in the quarter from last year's quarter to nearly $2 billion. The company said large corporate, government and educational accounts led the gains.

Dell's quarterly European sales, which made up 22 percent of its total revenues, grew 42 percent over last year's quarter to $620 million. The company said its operations in France and Germany posted year-over-year revenue growth of 46 percent, while its largest European business unit in the United Kingdom grew 37 percent.

Dell's desktop computers sales made up 73 percent of total revenues, down from 80 percent the year before. Sales of portable computers made up 19 percent of revenues, up from 17 percent. Server sales grew 299 percent year-on-year and made up eight percent of total revenues in the second quarter, up from three percent in 1996.
Dell said its Internet web site is now generating more than $2 million in sales per day.

Dell said it generated $289 million in cash from operations, increasing its cash and marketable securities to $1.5 billion at the close of the quarter. The company spent about $200 million to buy back 5.7 million of its shares during the quarter.
The computer maker said it has bought back 59.3 million shares since it started the 100-milion repurchase program 18 months ago and has contractual arrangements covering another 27 million shares.
Dell's operating expenses grew to 11.6 percent from 10.9 percent in the first quarter, as the company hired 1,600 new employees in the second quarter.
